claims.text: Replacing EAM references with a neural-network interatomic potential trained on solid and liquid ab initio configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
The neural-network reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by an estimated 25–50% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed method applies to equiatomic or near-equiatomic high-entropy alloys containing 5–7 components.
The proposed temperature range is approximately 1800–2500 K, near the alloys' melting temperatures.
The neural-network potential should be trained on ab initio datasets spanning solid and disordered-liquid configurations around the melting point.
Representing many-body and local atomic-configuration variations in the disordered liquid will mediate improved phase-space mapping between the reference and target systems.
Atomic environments vary widely in the disordered liquid state.
Traditional EAM potentials have a fixed functional form.
A neural-network potential has a flexible functional form trained on ab initio data.
The neural network's functional flexibility enables interpolation across a wider range of atomic configurations than the EAM reference.
Interpolation across a wider configuration range reduces mismatch between the reference and ab initio potential-energy landscapes during thermodynamic integration.
The neural-network reference will produce free energies closer to full ab initio results than the EAM-based TOR-TILD reference.
Using the neural-network reference will decrease computational uncertainty.
Using the neural-network reference will improve the accuracy of free-energy predictions.
Using the neural-network reference will improve the accuracy of melting-temperature predictions.
The efficacy of the neural-network reference depends on the completeness of its training dataset.
Failure to include rare but important liquid configurations in training can make the mismatch reduction less robust.
Extreme compositions with unconventional chemical ordering may challenge the neural-network approach.
Elemental and binary calculations provide preliminary indications that machine-learning potentials improve phase-space overlap.
A reduction of less than 10% in path mismatch, or failure to improve agreement with direct ab initio free energies relative to EAM, will falsify the hypothesis.
